meta.title: The Night Key
meta.skill_frame: Literary text: work out why a character does something from what the story shows.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a third-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 3.10 and 4.25 on the two parts (48 and 57 words), 3.69 together. The load is one character and one act, with the reason printed in the second part and one key to track. That sits inside the grade 2-3 band and below the 4.1 floor, which measures 5.3 at its easiest.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for literary_text 3.1, band 3.1, sequence 1. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A hotel night porter who keeps a lost key quiet, built so one quiet act carries a clear motive.
source.avoided: No hotel name, street, town, or wage. No claim about what the manager would have done.

session.difficulty_basis: One character, one quiet act, and the reason carried by two details in the second part.

authoring_exceptions: Parts run 45-60 words instead of 100-200. At band 3.1 the text is short by design: two parts keep the session inside 12 minutes and the whole story stays visible on one screen. Recorded under 2.1.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The night porter locks the front door of the hotel at eleven. Then he walks the halls and checks every room on the ground floor. In his coat he keeps one spare key. That key fits the side door by the bins, and nobody else has a copy.
passage.part_2: The cleaner lost her own key last month, and she told nobody. The porter did not report the loss to the manager. He cut a new key at his own cost and gave it to her before her shift. Now the side door opens at four in the morning, and the front door stays locked until six.

items.prompt: What does the porter keep in his coat?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He keeps one spare key.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The sentence about his coat says he keeps one spare key there.
tutor_only.tell: The porter carries one spare key in his coat, and it fits the side door.
help: The sentence about his coat says what he keeps in it.
It is a key, and there is one of them.
accept_ideas: the spare key for the side door
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the front door key
if_they_say.ask: The passage says this key fits a different door. Which door does it fit?

items.prompt: Which door does the spare key fit?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. It fits the side door by the bins.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The sentence after the one about his coat names the side door by the bins.
tutor_only.tell: The key in his coat fits the side door by the bins, not the front door.
help: The sentence about the key names the door it fits.
It is the door near the bins.
tutor_only.core_idea: The side door by the bins.
accept_ideas: the side door by the bins
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the front door
if_they_say.ask: The front door is the one he locks at eleven. Which door does the key fit?

items.prompt: The cleaner lost her key and told nobody. Why did the porter say nothing to the manager?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He kept it quiet so she would not get in trouble.
tutor_only.correct_reason: He did not report the loss. He paid for a new key and gave it to her before her shift.
tutor_only.tell: Reporting the loss would have made trouble for the cleaner. The porter kept it quiet and paid for a new key.
help: The sentence about the manager says what the porter did not do.
Instead of reporting her, he made her a new key.
tutor_only.core_idea: He wanted to help her instead of getting her in trouble.
accept_ideas: so she would not get in trouble
he did not want to report her
to keep her out of trouble
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he was afraid of the manager
if_they_say.ask: The passage says nothing about the manager being angry. What did the porter do instead of reporting?

items.prompt: The passage says nobody else has a copy of the porter's key. What does that show about how he works?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. He is careful about who can get into the building.
tutor_only.correct_reason: He checks every room on the ground floor and keeps the only spare key, so he controls who gets in.
tutor_only.tell: He walks the halls, checks the rooms, and holds the only spare key. That is a careful way to guard a building.
help: Look at what he does on his rounds before the key is named.
He checks the rooms, and only he holds the spare.
tutor_only.core_idea: He is careful about who can get into the building.
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he does not trust the cleaner
if_they_say.ask: He gives the cleaner a key of her own. What does the passage say about the key in his coat?

items.prompt: The porter paid for the new key himself. What does that show about why he helped the cleaner?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He helped her without wanting anything back.
tutor_only.correct_reason: He paid the cost himself and told no one, so the help was not for money or praise.
tutor_only.tell: He paid for the key and told nobody. He helped the cleaner without wanting anything in return.
help: Look at who paid and who was told.
Nobody paid him back, and the manager never heard of it.
tutor_only.core_idea: He helped her without wanting anything in return.
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says he wanted a reward
if_they_say.ask: The passage says he paid the cost himself and told nobody. Where would a reward come from?
